title: Club Growth Path
axisLabel: Club age — the typical order, not a required one
placeholder: Click any stage for what it involves and the one condition that has to be true before you move on. Drag the amber marker to where your club actually is.

items.label: Single site
items.hint: The founding year. No growth decision needed yet.
detail: One venue, one session, and the first three students through a pilot cohort.
Nothing about growth. The work of this stage is proving the session is worth attending twice.
There is no gate on this one — clubs leave this stage by having more students want in than the current session holds.

items.label: Scaling
items.hint: More students, more sessions, more mentors — all at one site.
detail: Growth in place: more students, more sessions, more mentors, still one venue.
Everything gets harder at once — the rota, the kit, the tracker — and none of it needs a second building.
A stable mentor pipeline. A club that is still recruiting mentors one at a time cannot staff a second site, and opening one will cost it the first.

items.label: Multi-site
items.hint: A second venue, run by a trained assistant leader.
detail: A second venue, run by somebody the club trained rather than by the founder commuting between two rooms.
The original site must have survived a leadership transition already. If it has never run without the founder, it will not run without the founder while the founder is at the other site.
A single excellent site serving forty students is not a lesser outcome than two struggling ones.

items.label: Franchise
items.hint: Somebody else's club, using your charter and curriculum.
detail: An independently run club elsewhere, starting from this club's charter and curriculum as a template.
What you are actually giving away
Documents, not oversight. A franchise you keep control of is a second site with extra paperwork.
It requires a charter and a curriculum good enough for a stranger to run from — which most clubs never write down, because they never had to.
